 Almaty R2 previews and predictions: Rublev vs. Mannarino, Tsitsipas vs. Kukushkin 
 October 21, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 10 
 Second-round competition in Almaty gets underway on Wednesday, when seeds Andrey Rublev and Stefanos Tsitsipas take the court. They are going up against Adrian Mannarino and Mikhail Kukushkin, respectively. 
 Adrian Mannarino vs. (4) Andrey Rublev 
 Rublev and Mannarino will be facing each other for the sixth time in their careers when they collide in round two of the Almaty Open on Wednesday. The head-to-head series stands at 4-1 in Rublev’s favor after the Russian prevailed at Wimbledon in 2025. Mannarino can take confidence from the fact that his lone win has come on an indoor hard court — 5-7, 7-6(4), 6-3 at the 2021 Moscow event. However, Rublev won their other two indoor encounters in Moscow (2019) and Astana (2022).
Whereas Rublev earned a first-round bye as the No. 4 seed, Mannarino kicked off his week with a 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-3 victory over Aleksandar Vukic on Monday. As usual, the 38-year-old Frenchman is heating up during the fall swing — this time with a quarterfinal performance in Chengdu and a third-round showing at the Shanghai Masters. Meanwhile, Rublev is just 7-7 in his last 14 matches dating back to the post-Wimbledon clay-court stretch in July. When you aren’t playing well, Mannarino is not the kind of opponent you want to see on the other side of the net — especially not on an indoor hard court.
 Pick: Mannarino in 3

 (7) Stefanos Tsitsipas vs. (WC) Mikhail Kukushkin
Kukushkin is retiring in front how the home crowd in Kazakhstan this week. The 38-year-old treated his fans to a 7-6(4), 7-6(3) win over qualifier Stefanos Sakellaridis on Monday, and it will probably be the last one his career given that a much different Stefanos awaits him on Wednesday. It was also Kukushkin’s first victory at the ATP level in more than two years (Hangzhou in 2024), which is why he is down at No. 389 in the rankings.
This marks the sixth showdown between Tsitsipas and Kukushkin, with the Greek sweeping the head-to-head series 5-0 (4-0 on the main tour). Their most recent contest also came in Kazakhstan, where Tsitsipas cruised 6-3, 6-4 at the 2022 Astana event. The world No. 39 opened this week with a 7-6(9), 3-6, 6-3 defeat of Aleksandar Kovacevic on Monday, improving to 12-3 in his last 15 matches. Kukushkin did extremely well to advance one round in his final tournament, but this is almost certainly the end of the road.
 Pick: Tsitsipas in 2
